continuation_check.process_scope: Only node/postgres/pg_ctl commands containing checkpoint-idempotency-db or clued-checkpoint-idempotency-

findings_resolved.finding: Old same (owner,binding,key) replay ignored effective payload and context.
findings_resolved.evidence: Independent execution reproduced changed summary/context returning the old duplicate before applying the migration.
findings_resolved.repair: Compare context, original receipt-backed base_version, JSONB snapshot and normalized summary/next_action. Mismatches return idempotency_key_conflict without checkpoint/receipt writes.

findings_resolved.finding: Old JSON null base_version bypassed SQL CAS inequality.
findings_resolved.evidence: Independent execution reproduced a successful old null-base commit.
findings_resolved.repair: Reject null/negative bases; bigint maximum conflicts without arithmetic overflow.

findings_resolved.finding: version-1 cannot prove the original input base for historical null-base commits.
findings_resolved.evidence: A pre-migration null-base checkpoint cannot be replayed with an invented version-minus-one base.
findings_resolved.repair: Require exactly one original immutable checkpoint audit receipt with non-null base_version; do not backfill or edit old evidence.

verified_behaviors: Same effective legacy payload with a new valid session replays the exact old checkpoint; normalized surrounding whitespace and JSONB key order are equivalent.
Changing context/base_version/snapshot/summary/next_action conflicts with no new checkpoint or checkpoint receipt.
Borrowing another binding's session is denied with SQLSTATE 42501.
Separate legitimate bindings and users retain independent idempotency namespaces; existing stream CAS still applies.
Concurrent same-key/same-payload produces exactly one checkpoint and one duplicate response.
Concurrent same key across two authorized contexts produces one commit and one conflict.
Ended/expired sessions and a revoked binding cannot replay.
Applying the migration again preserves the selected historical checkpoint, immutable receipt and existing function grants.

static_review.surface: One CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION; no row rewrite, table/schema grant expansion, credential change or new idempotency namespace.
static_review.authorization: Existing resolve_binding and resolve_session remain before replay lookup; anon-role tests use those actual repository RPC functions.
static_review.serialization: Transaction advisory lock uses existing owner/binding/key namespace, so cross-context attempts with the same key serialize before lookup.
static_review.legacy_evidence: Original base is read from existing audit metadata; missing/ambiguous/null evidence is not fabricated from checkpoint version.

limitations: This is independent real local PostgreSQL regression and code review, not production deployment or a live Clued/OAuth end-to-end verification.
The test uses synthetic auth fixtures and selected repository migrations matching the affected function chain.
No R11, Entry, full Slice A, model or human-efficiency acceptance is issued.
